title: Troubleshooting Windows driver problems

spans.caption: A diagram of the lesson’s key ideas

spans.text: A driver is software that helps the operating system communicate with a printer, graphics card, Wi-Fi adapter, or other device. A driver problem can make a device disappear, interrupt sound, or show an error.

Open Device Manager, find the affected device, and read its status. Record any warning icon and error code. Restart the computer and check simple causes such as cables, power, or a Wi-Fi switch. Ask whether other users are affected.

Check Windows Update and the manufacturer’s official support page. Select a driver for the exact computer model; a driver for another model can make the problem worse. Avoid unknown “driver updater” apps and advertising links.
If the problem began after an update

If the issue started immediately after a driver update, check whether Device Manager offers “Roll Back Driver,” or install a previous version approved by the manufacturer. Before changing anything, check the restore plan and have the BitLocker recovery key available when needed.

After a change, restart and test the device in its real task. Record the error code, model, driver version, and actions taken. If it still fails, or affects security or work, hand it to the support team; do not remove drivers at random.
